articles.title: Rupee likely to open flat as dollar strength, US bond yields weigh on sentiment
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee is expected to open largely flat against the US dollar on Monday amid mixed global cues.

The Indian rupee is expected to open largely flat on Monday, caught between higher US bond yields, dollar strength and volatile oil prices, while a revival in foreign portfolio inflows cushions the pressure.

The rupee is expected to open in the 94.22 to 94.28 range, according to traders, having settled at 94.24 to the dollar on Friday.

The currency, which had been on a winning run, came under pressure late last week, largely weighed down by a surge in US Treasury yields that lifted the dollar index to its highest level in a year and a half.

articles.title: Rupee rises 43 paise to close at 93.51 (provisional) against US dollar
articles.excerpt:
The rupee appreciated by 43 paise to close at 93.51 against the US dollar on Tuesday, on the back of softer crude oil prices, upbeat domestic markets, and foreign fund inflows even as a strong dollar and elevated US bond yields limited the upside.

Forex traders said fresh foreign fund inflows and softer crude oil prices are supporting the rupee, while a stronger dollar and rising US yields remain key risks.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.72 against the dollar. During intra-day trade, it hit a high of 93.40 and a low of 93.73. The local unit settled at 93.51 (provisional), higher by 43 paise from its previous close.

articles.title: Robust inflows, pullback in shorts lift rupee to seven-month peak
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee saw a notable rise, achieving its peak value in seven months following a surge in foreign equity investments. Closing at 93.47 per dollar, this upswing was driven by an impressive influx of $10 billion this month. Additionally, traders observed substantial movements in the dollar-rupee non-deliverable forward market as bearish positions were unwound.

articles.title: Boris Vujčić: Risks and resilience in the euro area financial system
articles.excerpt:
It is my great pleasure to open this year's Frankfurt Euro Finance Week. This event provides a timely opportunity to reflect on the state of the euro area financial system and the challenges ahead. articles.title: Yen steady against euro and dollar after soft Japanese GDP data
articles.excerpt:
SINGAPORE, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The yen was pinned near two-month lows against the dollar and little moved against the euro in early trade on Monday as markets assessed how an unexpected contraction in the Japanese economy in the third quarter affects the policy outlook.

The yen fluctuated between gains and losses without moving too far, trading against the dollar at 159.69 yen and against the euro at 176.04 yen, close to levels where US and Japanese authorities are believed to have intervened earlier this year.

articles.excerpt:
